title: NY State Senate · District 17
area: Southwest Brooklyn, including Bay Ridge, Bensonhurst, Dyker Heights and parts of Sunset Park.

context.text: Incumbent Steve Chan won a 2025 special election to fill the seat, succeeding Democrat Iwen Chu. Both the Democratic and Republican primaries for this seat were canceled for 2026, with each candidate advancing unopposed to the general election.

summary.text: Steve Chan is the Republican, Conservative and "Stop Mamdani Party" candidate for NY State Senate District 17 in southwest Brooklyn, a retired NYPD sergeant and Marine Corps veteran who won a 2025 special election, flipping the seat from Democratic control. He is seeking a full term against Democrat Larry He.

background.text: Born in Hong Kong; immigrated to the United States at age 11 and settled in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, where he has lived for 47 years, including 32 years in Bensonhurst.
Attended PS 102 in Bay Ridge, JHS 259 William McKinley, and Fort Hamilton High School, then SUNY Empire State College.
Served six years in the United States Marine Corps (1984–1990).
Served 27 years in the NYPD (1993–2020), retiring as a sergeant; operated a small florist shop in Sunset Park for 10 years while on the force and volunteered as a notary for neighbors.
Married with two daughters; volunteered 10 years in two public schools, including as PTA president and Title I chair.

priorities.text: Describes himself as accessible rather than a career politician, saying he is fighting to stop what he calls decline in the city and state.
priorities.quote: I'm not a politician. I'm not looking for a job. I'm here to fight for us, our community, our city, our state. I'm here to stop the madness that is turning New York into dystopia.

priorities.text: Lists public safety, cashless bail, wasteful government spending, e-bike enforcement, illegal immigration, education, cost of living, health care, taxes, congestion pricing, and services for seniors and veterans as the issues he is focused on.
Says the first bill he would introduce is to provide qualified immunity for police officers.

positions.summary: Voted no on the GREAT Act (S9500-A), a statewide virtual power plant program intended to reduce reliance on fossil-fuel peaker plants, and no on S7898-A, which requires certain construction contracts to site renewable-energy and energy-storage systems.

record.text: Serves as ranking member on the Cities 1 and New York City Education committees; also serves on the Commerce, Economic Development and Small Business, Education, and Investigations and Government Operations committees.

Sponsored S9441, requiring landlords of one- to six-family rental dwellings in New York City to provide fire extinguishers in rented apartments; passed the Senate 60–0 on June 4, 2026 and remained pending in the Assembly Housing Committee.

Sponsored S10236, which would bar local governments from requiring businesses to replace existing storefront security gates or grilles solely for transparency or visual-access standards; remained in the Senate Consumer Protection Committee as of May 7, 2026.

Sponsored S10353, which would direct the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority to discount Verrazano-Narrows Bridge tolls to 70% of the regular fare for Kings County residents using personal vehicles; remained in the Senate Transportation Committee as of May 14, 2026.

Sponsored S9938, which would impose mandatory prison sentences for certain offenses committed on public transportation and create a new felony offense of reckless endangerment on public transportation; remained in the Senate Codes Committee as of April 16, 2026.
Voted no on S9500-A (GREAT Act), establishing the New York State grid reliability and energy affordability transition program, which passed the Senate 39–21.

Voted no on S7898-A, requiring certain construction project contracts to include siting of renewable energy systems, energy storage systems or electric major utility transmission facilities, which passed the Senate 39–21.
Voted no on S10585, which assesses a separate tax on distributions from designated settlement funds, which passed the Senate 39–21.

summary.text: Larry He is the Democratic candidate for NY State Senate District 17, a first-time candidate and Brooklyn Democratic district leader who serves as chief of staff to State Assemblyman William Colton.

background.text: A first-generation immigrant and Brooklyn Democratic district leader.

Serves as chief of staff to State Assemblyman William Colton, work he describes as bringing food pantries, neighborhood cleanups, senior services, legal assistance, immigration support, and small-business and nonprofit aid directly into the district.
Endorsed by Assemblyman William Colton and New York City Councilmember Susan Zhuang.

priorities.text: Lists safer and cleaner neighborhoods, affordable living and lower taxes, and faster and more accessible transit as his three key campaign messages.
Says he is personally passionate about affordability, public safety, education and quality-of-life issues.

researchNotes: Larry He is a first-time candidate whose only substantial public statements found are his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers; no campaign website content beyond that survey, and no statements mapping to the fixed issue list, were found, so his positions list is empty rather than inferred. Chan's positions beyond climate rely on floor votes; his 2024 survey answers list several issues he says he is focused on without always stating a clear for/against stance on the specific fixed-issue wording, so only the vote-backed climate position is included as a formal Position.
